instructions: Drain the chickpeas and pat them very dry with a clean towel. Leave them uncovered for 20 minutes while the oven heats.
Put the chickpeas on a large baking sheet and toss them with half the oil. Roast for 20 minutes.
Add the barley and the rest of the oil to the sheet. Stir once and roast for 15 minutes.
Add the peanuts and roast for 8 to 10 minutes, until everything smells toasty and a few grains of barley are crunchy when you bite one.
Transfer everything to a bowl and stir in the salt while it's hot. Spread it out on the baking sheet and let it cool completely.
Put the kolo in a jar or a bowl. Sprinkle the berbere over your own portion if you want some heat.
Serve at room temperature. Once it's fully cool, it keeps in a sealed jar for up to 1 week.
method_notes: The sources agree that kolo is barley, peanuts and chickpeas roasted until crunchy and seasoned with salt and berbere. The World on a Plate (the lead) roasts everything in the oven, while Ethiopian Food dry roasts in a pan with dried chickpeas, and Made in Hackney boils the grains first. None of the three pages showed a rating, so the lead is the most detailed method I read. This follows The World on a Plate at about 40 percent of its amounts, with canned chickpeas, and the berbere is kept for the table.
